content.title: Wizards Acquire Four-Time All-Star Trae Young | Washington Wizards
content.text: Juju Reese feels right at home playing for the Wizards and not just because it's the closest NBA team to where he grew up.ORLANDO, FL - MARCH 3: Julian Reese #15 of the Washington Wizards and Angel Reese pose for a photo after the game against the Orlando Magic on March 3, 2026 at Kia Center in Orlando, Florida. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Fernando Medina/NBAE via Getty Images)WASHINGTON – The University of Maryland is just 30 miles away from Capital One Arena, and the Terps send plenty of players to the NBA, yet very few in recent decades have gone on to play for the Wizards. It’s surprising in part because it used to be a thing.In the mid-2000s, the Wizards at one point could boast not one, not two, but all three stars from the Terrapins’ 2002 national title team; Juan Dixon, Steve Blake and Lonny Baxter. But after Dixon’s second stint with the franchise ended in 2009, only one Terp – Alex Len – played for the Wizards across a 17-year span (per Real GM).That changed last week when the Wizards signed forward Juju Reese to a two-way contract, luring him away from the Raptors 905 after he went undrafted following a four-year career in College Park. Reese has already made his mark for the Wizards with a game of 18 points and 20 rebounds against the Jazz, setting a rookie franchise record for offensive rebounds (10) and pulling in the most boards for any Washington rookie since 1992 (Tom Gugliotta).Reese, 22, grew up in nearby Baltimore and stayed home to play at Maryland in part to play in front of family. Now he gets to do that in the pros.“Pretty much any team would have gotten me excited, but even more that it’s at home. I’m just glad to be back home and playing for my hometown. My mom can come to games,” Reese told Monumental Sports Network.Reese’s mother, Angel, was indeed there for his NBA debut on Monday against the Rockets. The next night, in Orlando, had his sister sitting courtside wearing his jersey.Reese’s sister, also Angel, is a household name as one of the most famous players in the WNBA. Juju said Angel texts him before and after every game with pointers. She’ll even try to reach him at halftime.Angel certainly has some wisdom to impart following an illustrious college career and now as a WNBA All-Star. They also happen to have similar games as power forwards known for their rebounding.“I’m really happy for him,” Angel told Monumental Sports Network’s Meghan McPeak. “I was so emotional when I found out, I was crying so hard like I just hit the lottery. I was just so happy because my mom was able to raise me and my brother, we were able to go to Maryland and play in front of our family.”Angel, of course, transferred to LSU midway through her college career. Juju, on the other hand, played all four years, sticking around even amid a coaching change. The head coach who recruited him, Mark Turgeon, was fired midway through Reese’s freshman season.That was one hurdle Reese had to overcome to make it to the NBA and few can attest better than Eric Ayala, who was a senior when Reese arrived as a freshman at Maryland and took him under his wing.Ayala happened to sign with the Capital City Go-Go, the Wizards’ G League affiliate, just weeks before Reese followed him. The two talk often enough that when Reese called Ayala with the news, he didn’t think anything of it.Reese used that to his advantage, starting the conversation by reminiscing about their Maryland days.“Don’t you miss me being on your team and hooping together,” Reese asked to build suspense. Then, he delivered the news.Ayala was happy to be teammates with Reese again and also to see him culminate his journey to the NBA. He saw up close how hard Reese worked to get stronger, improve his shot and heed lessons from an evolving coaching staff.Ayala was impressed right away with Reese’s work ethic and how often he would see him in the gym. Reese was a quiet, but diligent freshman who was willing to listen to advice and take constructive criticism.Then the games began and one moment against the University of Illinois opened Ayala’s eyes. Ayala was posting up against Kofi Cockburn, a big man listed at 7 feet and 293 pounds, when he found Reese with a pass on the baseline.“I throw it to him and Juju bumps on Kofi and then after that, Juju just kind of [got] all the confidence he needed, like ‘I belong here,’” Ayala said over the phone.“That was something where like we went back to the locker room and were like ‘bro, you [dunked] on him!’”Now that Reese is back in the area and in close proximity to Maryland, he can be more connected to his alma mater. Just days after signing with the Wizards, he was spotted at the Maryland-Rutgers game last weekend.“It feels good, especially going there I get so much love. It’s just a great feeling, seeing the impact I left there,” Reese said.Ayala isn’t the only player in the Wizards organization whom Reese has reunited with. He also has ties to both Bub Carrington and Cam Whitmore having grown up in Baltimore and being around the same age.Reese is two years older than Carrington and, while they attended the same high school at St. Frances Academy, they did not overlap as teammates. Carrington made sure to clear that up after some on social media suggested otherwise.They instead got to know each other well through mutual friends and by seeing each other at basketball camps over the years.“I’ve just known him my entire life,” Carrington told Monumental Sports Network.While Reese made the call to Ayala, it was Carrington who pinged Reese first after news began circulating they would be teammates in the NBA. Two kids from Baltimore, now playing for the same NBA franchise just one hour south of where they grew up.Carrington, 20, takes a lot of pride in being from Baltimore.“My reaction was ‘we got another one, B-more stand up!’ Obviously, well-deserved for him as well. Nobody works as hard as him. I’ve seen enough of his journey to know that it’s well-deserved and I’m happy he’s here,” Carrington said.Angel mentioned Carrington in her interview with McPeak on the Wizards-Magic broadcast and an interaction they had before the game. Angel told him to throw her brother some lobs and Carrington said they’ve already been working on it.The Baltimore connection is strong for the Wizards right now and Angel counts herself a fan.“I’m really excited for DMV hoops. D.C. is back, we’ve got some great picks, Trae Young is coming in, [Anthony Davis]; so I’m really happy for D.C.,” she said.
